requirements.requirement: Establish an integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (install/configure a file-integrity tool and initialize a database covering /etc)
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed (cmd-13da7a288c0b46ab), the default AlmaLinux 9 aide.conf ruleset covering /etc with specific NORMAL/CONTENT rules plus a recursive '/etc PERMS' catch-all was confirmed (cmd-9e8981065c994b4a, cmd-da9fb10799b54a2a), and 'aide --init' produced a 28662-entry database activated as the live /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz (cmd-7f8e0daad63048b2, cmd-e48fe62db698497e). A subsequent clean 'aide --check' confirmed the baseline matched the filesystem (cmd-0841058ba3d0434b).

requirements.requirement: The baseline must allow later changes to /etc files to be identified and reported
requirements.summary: A deliberate append to /etc/hosts and removal of /etc/motd were both correctly flagged by 'aide --check' with size/hash diffs and a removed-entry report (cmd-10c13beef73045f9), directly demonstrating detection and reporting capability for later /etc changes.

requirements.requirement: Leave the system in a clean, accurate final state after any test mutations
requirements.summary: After the falsification test, /etc/hosts content was restored and /etc/motd was recreated, then a fresh 'aide --init' produced a clean final baseline matching the true current state, confirmed with a no-differences 'aide --check' (cmd-a5068464c81b48f2, cmd-2b6082f8df184230, cmd-c6f07893addb43a8). Note: /etc/motd was recreated as a 0-byte file via 'touch' rather than restored to its original content, since the pre-test content was never captured — a minor imprecision, but since the final baseline was re-initialized from current state, the AIDE database itself is internally consistent and functional regardless of motd's exact byte content.

requirements.requirement: (Independent) provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (4a743885...), uptime, aide.db.gz md5sum, and a clean aide --check were captured (cmd-042bd62415564aa5), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned an acknowledgement before disconnection (cmd-8207adeb48404642). A subsequent poll hit a connection timeout mid-reboot (cmd-991b901fa8ac4986), then succeeded with a new boot_id f4ea82c9... (cmd-dd7070059e014be4), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot and the executor_comparison diff. Post-restart, the aide.db.gz md5sum was unchanged, aide package remained installed, and 'aide --check' again reported no differences (cmd-fc010fa350ac4129), confirming full recovery of the integrity-monitoring state.

overall_summary: The executor installed AIDE, established a full /etc-covering integrity baseline, and directly demonstrated its change-detection/reporting capability via a controlled falsification test before restoring a clean final baseline. The independent node-restart protocol was also completed with direct before/after evidence of boot identity change and full recovery of the AIDE database and monitoring state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good; the only minor issue is that /etc/motd's pre-test content wasn't captured before mutation, so its exact restoration can't be confirmed (though this has no material effect on the integrity baseline's correctness).
limitations: Pre-test content of /etc/motd was not captured before the falsification test, so it is not possible to confirm the recreated file exactly matches its original content — though this is low-impact since the final baseline was freshly re-initialized from actual current state.

No cron/timer integration for periodic 'aide --check' runs was found or configured (cmd-fe994c96edea45a0), meaning ongoing automated reporting is not yet wired up; the task instruction only required establishing the baseline itself, not scheduling periodic checks, so this is not scored as unsatisfied.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor mutations were tied to a clear purpose: installing AIDE (required), initializing/activating the baseline (required), a bounded falsification test on /etc/hosts and /etc/motd to demonstrate detection capability (reasonable verification of the task's stated goal of identifying/reporting future changes, fully reverted), a required restart for the mandatory node-restart protocol, and reinitializing a clean final baseline. No residue, failed services, unsafe exposure, or package-state damage appears in the after_executor lifecycle snapshot versus after_prepare — only expected reboot-related diffs (new boot_id, new chronyd/sshd PIDs, new systemd-private temp dirs, /tmp/reboot.log from the backgrounded shutdown command). One minor imprecision: /etc/motd was recreated via 'touch' (0 bytes) rather than restored to its exact pre-test content, since original content was never captured before the test (cmd-2b6082f8df184230) — low-risk since motd is a non-sensitive banner file and the final aide --init re-baselines from actual current state either way.
